extracted.intended_audience: writers, students of composition, and literary critics interested in principles of literary style
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for assessing and producing literary style across genres (from mathematical exposition to poetry), emphasizing appropriateness of language, author's presence, word-choice, ordering of images, and economy of reader's attention. Useful for critiquing prose and verse for naturalness, originality, and expressive power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of language complexity to subject
rubrics_metrics.description: The less the author's personality is involved in the matter treated, the simpler the language which suffices; algebra and mathematical proof are perfectly dispassionate and require simple, adequate language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match language complexity to objectivity or subjectivity of subject matter. Anti-pattern: applying ornate or highly-personal diction to purely objective, technical subjects where simple, dispassionate language is adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict use of scientific/technical terminology in exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The terminology of science is found very tolerably sufficient, if strictly adhered to, and mostly where expository and descriptive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In scientific and expository writing, prefer precise technical terms and adhere to established usage rather than rhetorical embellishment; this preserves adequacy and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility of the author's personality (style as character)
rubrics_metrics.description: Style may be provisionally accepted which identifies it with character — with unconscious revelations of the hidden self; the author's personality creeps in and emerges in epithets, repetitions, and phrases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how the unconscious traits and life-experiences of the author shape the writing. Value is placed on the authentic, characteristic touches that reveal a writer's individuality rather than generic, imitative phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision and weight of word choice (especially in poetry)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a very fine passage every word is charged with meaning and riveted to its place; Coleridge's definition: 'the best words in the best order.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require economy and exactness in word-selection; each word should carry significance and be positioned deliberately. Anti-pattern: wasted or ornamental words that dilute poetic or rhetorical force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of rhetorical figures (epithet, simile, metaphor) as refinements
rubrics_metrics.description: Delicate implications of expression are embodied in all the recognized figures of rhetoric, the trope, the simile, and the metaphor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether rhetorical figures illuminate aspects of fact and convey the author's perspective rather than merely decorate; good usage integrates figures into the reader's experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection, combination and ordering of images (gradation and transition)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is the mode of their combination into a definite picture, the order in which the images follow one another, and the gradation and transition of ideas which are all part of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the sequencing and layering of images and ideas for organic flow and effective buildup (example: sensory impressions moving from distance to close). Anti-pattern: disordered or abrupt image transitions that confuse rather than reveal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing sensory detail to create reader experience
rubrics_metrics.description: The smell of cedar, and the voice of the divine songstress... are, by the epithets 'fragrant' and 'sweet,' made part of the real or imagined experience of the poet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer evocative, sensory language that makes scenes experiential for the reader. Contrast with a bare statement (e.g., 'there were birds') which lacks the same evocative force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial restraint appropriate to narrative (withdrawal vs intrusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not that this personality is directly obtruded upon the hearer's notice; in the instance of Homer, it is markedly withdrawn, the characters speak of themselves, the descriptions are meant to serve no moral end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the author appropriately withdraws or asserts presence. In many narratives effective restraint — letting characters and scenes speak — is preferable to overt authorial moralizing or intrusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalness and authenticity of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: The happiest touches are those which are original — those phrases and expressions are most welcome... which set the matter they convey in a new light — and that the light in which the writer himself sees it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor passages that feel natural to the author and reveal a genuine perspective. Anti-pattern: mannered or forced 'stylishness' that betrays affectation rather than authentic vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of the reader's attention (devices to direct focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: The various devices of language do serve to the economy of the reader's attention, and that beauties of style are beauties partly because they effect this end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess rhetorical and compositional devices by how effectively they direct and conserve reader attention — clarity of focus, well-managed emphasis, and purposeful ornamentation count positively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of expression over originality of idea
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality is far oftener originality of expression than idea, a fresh aspect of something old, not a discovery of something new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value new phrasing, fresh perspectives, and distinctive presentation even when the underlying idea is familiar. Anti-pattern: recycling old ideas in stale, conventional language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of perception and expression outranks quantity of information
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not so much what a man knows as how he knows it, not so much the extent as the quality of his information, that gains him a right to be heard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating prose, weight the writer's expressive acuity and the refinement of insight over mere breadth or volume of facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style as individuality and differentiation (value of distinct voice)
rubrics_metrics.description: The distinguishing feature [of power of expression] is its individuality... the superiority of genius in degree is mainly a consequence of its difference in kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the distinctiveness of voice and idiosyncratic perspective as positive marks of style; sameness and uniformity are criticized.
